meta.title: Analysis of LLMs Against Prompt Injection and Jailbreak Attacks

problem.v: Vulnerability of small/medium open-source LLMs to prompt injection and jailbreaks, and whether lightweight inference-time defences help without retraining
problem.q: empirically investigates vulnerabilities in open-source LLMs related to prompt injection

main_idea.v: Evaluate 10 open-source LLMs on 91 injection + 74 jailbreak prompts, then 5 inference-time defences on 6 models; human-judged vulnerability
main_idea.q: 10 open-source LLMs across 91 prompt injection and 74 jailbreak attack scenarios

threat_model.v: Black-box prompting of locally runnable open models; no retraining; resource-constrained deployments

datasets_benchmarks.name: Curated adversarial prompts (Reddit, Discord, GitHub repos, public datasets, papers)

metrics.name: Vulnerability rate (%) judged by humans; timeouts and empty responses tracked

results.claim: Prompt-injection vulnerability: qwen3:1.7b 71.3%, gemma3:1b 62.8%, DeepSeek-R1:1.5b 34.0%, Llama3.2:1b 30.9%; six larger models 0%
results.confidence: medium (model order in flattened Table 3 inferred)

results.claim: Jailbreak (74 prompts) vulnerable counts: gemma3:1b 49, Llama3.2:3b 36, qwen3:1.7b 8, Llama3.2:1b 7, DeepSeek-R1:1.5b 1, qwen3:4b 0
results.q: DeepSeek-R1:1.5B is the most robust, with only 1.37% vulnerability

results.claim: 0% injection vulnerability does not imply jailbreak robustness
results.q: Llama3.2:3B showed 0% injection vulnerability but 69.2% jailbreak vulnerability

results.claim: Defence ranking: Self-Defence best; Input Filtering weakest (Llama3.2 3B ~42% vulnerable); System Prompt inconsistent (~39% for Llama3.2 3B); Vector 25-30%; Voting 13-15% on small models
results.q: Input Filtering emerges as the weakest defence
Weak judge models (e.g., Gemma3:1B) approve up to 49.7% of unsafe outputs

limitations_stated.v: Defences are bypassed by long reasoning-heavy prompts
limitations_stated.q: consistently bypassed by long, reasoning-heavy prompts

limitations_stated.v: Jailbreak/defended runs limited to fewer models due to instability and compute

limitations_inferred: [INFERENCE] Direct prompting only; no RAG/indirect injection, tools, or cloud deployment
[INFERENCE] Rates lack confidence intervals; denominators inconsistent (see flags)
[INFERENCE] Closest prior work to our brief; our novelty must differ (RAG/tool apps, CIs, deterministic success checks, cloud deployment)

artifacts.note: paper claims public release of dataset; no URL found in text

reusable_for_our_project.v: Model shortlist known to run on modest hardware (Llama3.2 1b/3b, qwen3, gemma3, DeepSeek-R1 1.5b, phi3, Mistral 7b); five defence baselines to re-implement; attack categories

flags: Table 3 labelled /91 but 67 vulnerable -> 71.3% implies denominator 94 (67/91=73.6%)
Jailbreak rates use inconsistent denominators (gemma3:1b ~67%=49/74; Llama3.2:3B 69.2%=36/52 completed)
Judged by humans (p12) - no inter-rater stats found
